title: Launch scout
oneLiner: An agent that watches every new launch on higher.fun, rug-checks each one, writes a daily report of the few worth a look, and can make small capped buys in the ones that pass.
solToStart: 0 SOL, or about 0.3 SOL if it buys
howItWorks: Watches higher.fun's live feed for new launches, and lists the newest coins every few minutes in case the feed drops.
Waits an hour after each launch, then reads the coin: its rug check, holders, trades so far and the creator's other coins.
Scores it against rules you set in scout.config.json: the safety verdict, the creator's and top 10 holders' shares, how many wallets bought, and volume.
Writes a daily report, reports/<date>.md: the coins that passed and why, and the near misses.
If you turn buying on, it makes one small buy in a coin that passes (0.05 SOL to start), guards it with a stop-loss and a take-profit, and buys at most three a day.
earns: Reporting earns nothing and costs nothing on-chain. Buying can win or lose, and most new coins fall: a scout that buys a few a day will lose on most of them, and needs the rare big winner to come out ahead. Treat buying as a small, capped experiment, and read the calculator first.
costs: Reporting: nothing on-chain. It reads higher.fun's API and live feed.
Each buy and sell: the coin's trading fee (1% on a New school curve), Solana network fees, and Highwire's 0.3%.
Stop-losses and take-profits cost nothing until they fill.
needs: A machine that stays on, for the feed and the order runner
risks: New coins are the riskiest on higher.fun. Rug checks catch some bad launches, not all.
Coin names and descriptions are written by their creators and can be bait. The scout treats them as data and never follows them.
The policy can't allow-list coins that don't exist yet, so its caps per buy and per day are what limit the scout. Keep them small.
higher.fun's API refuses bursts of requests. The scout reads slowly and backs off.

milestones.title: M1 · Watching and scoring
milestones.summary: The live feed with a fallback, an hour's wait, and a score for each new coin, printed as it goes.

milestones.title: M2 · The daily report
milestones.summary: reports/<date>.md with the passes, the near misses and why, and unit tests for the scoring.

milestones.title: M3 · Buying, as a dry run
milestones.summary: With buying on: one capped buy per passing coin, then a stop-loss and a take-profit, all dry runs.

milestones.title: M4 · Going live (you)
milestones.summary: Read a week of reports, fund the wallet, and set live only if you still want it to buy.

prompt: Read PRD.md and AGENTS.md, then build milestone 1. Keep the policy a dry run: never set "live" yourself.

day.text: You deploy the template, run setup, and set your rules in scout.config.json. Buying is off.
The scout follows higher.fun's live feed. Each new launch goes on a list, to be read once it's an hour old.
It reads the coin: rug check, holders, trades. A coin with the creator holding 30% or a HIGH_RISK verdict fails; the score and the reasons go in the day's report.
reports/<date>.md is complete: every launch it saw, the few that passed, and why.
A coin that passes gets one 0.05 SOL buy, a stop-loss 30% below and a take-profit 100% above. At most three a day, as dry runs until you set the policy live.
Create the STOP file and nothing more is signed. Every buy, sell and refusal is in the audit log.

policyNotes.actions: Trades only: no launches, claims, posts or transfers.
policyNotes.max_sol_per_tx: The most one buy can spend: small, since every coin it buys is new.
policyNotes.max_sol_per_day: Three buys a day at most, whatever passes.
policyNotes.max_slippage_bps: 8%: new coins move fast in their first hours.
policyNotes.orders: Stop-losses and take-profits for the coins it bought, at most six open.

faq.q: Does it have to buy anything?
faq.a: No. Buying is off in scout.config.json, and the first two milestones only read and report. Many people will only ever run the report.

faq.q: Why wait an hour after a launch?
faq.a: A coin's first minutes say little: snipers, bundles and a creator selling show up in its holders and trades soon after. Waiting costs the very first moves, and avoids many of the worst.

faq.q: Can someone trick it into buying?
faq.a: It never reads instructions from a coin's name, description, comments or chat, and scores only on-chain facts and higher.fun's numbers. A creator can still game those, so the caps stay small.

faq.q: Why is there no allow-list in the policy?
faq.a: It buys coins that didn't exist when you wrote the policy. Highwire warns about a live policy that trades with no allow-list; here, the per-buy and per-day caps are the limit, so keep them small.

faq.q: Will it hit higher.fun's rate limits?
faq.a: It reads one coin at a time, a few seconds apart, and backs off when higher.fun refuses. The live feed does most of the watching.
Turn buying off in scout.config.json, create the STOP file (~/.highwire/launch-scout/STOP), or set the policy back to a dry run.
